summary: Kickoff for Starlight Health onboarding to Redwood. Reviewed roles, timeline, security and network requirements, discussed hosted vs private deployment options, and agreed on pilot scope. Agreed next steps and owners; technical deep dive and VPC checklist scheduled.
topics: Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Networking: VPC peering, firewall rules, egress
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay, welcome everyone, thanks for joining the kickoff. I'm Jordan from Redwood CSM team. Today we'll run through kickoff plan, roles, and next steps.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hi, thanks, Maya here. Excited to get started, we run patient triage workflows and want to integrate some summarization and clinical note generation.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya, SE. I'll be liaising on the network and deployment side, and I'll run the technical deep dive next week.
[00:37] Carlos Rivera: Carlos here, DevOps; main concerns are VPC peering, firewall egress and key management.
[00:50] Dr. Alan Brooks: Alan, clinical lead. We'll be responsible for clinical validation and acceptance criteria.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Great, quick agenda: introductions, go over timeline, decide deployment path (hosted vs private), security/compliance Qs, then pilot scope.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Our timeline is tight: pilot live in 6 weeks, production in three months. Success metrics: latency under 300ms for short prompts, cost per session targets, and clinical accuracy on summaries.
[01:34] Jordan Lee: That's doable. For latency, if you need sub-200ms we often recommend Redwood Dedicated or local private deployment, otherwise hosted is faster to start.
[01:46] Priya Nair: Just to add, with hosted you get immediate API access and we handle keys, but for PHI/regulated data we usually steer to Private (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed KMS.
[01:58] Carlos Rivera: We do handle PHI, so KMS and audit logs are must-haves. Also SSO with SAML and RBAC for our teams.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: Understood. We have SOC 2 Type II and support SSO/SAML, RBAC, with integration patterns in the security pack I'll share. Audit logs and per-request metadata are available in Redwood Console.
[02:26] Dr. Alan Brooks: A quick question — can you confirm data retention and whether logs containing PHI are masked or removed?
[02:35] Priya Nair: Current pattern: hosted customers can opt-in to data retention options; for Private you have full control — logs can be routed to your SIEM and KMS is customer-managed. I'll follow up with the security doc.
[02:48] Maya Chen: Also can we do an on-prem deployment later if the pilot requires it?
[02:54] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support a Private on-prem package. Usually customers start hosted for speed, then move to Private for compliance. That said, if you want to start Private we can scope the network and infra in parallel.
[03:08] Carlos Rivera: Network question — do you support VPC peering and what are the sticky ports and egress IPs?
[03:15] Priya Nair: We support VPC peering and private link options. We'll provide the CIDR, egress IP ranges, and firewall rules. We'll also share a terraform example.
[03:28] Jordan Lee: For the pilot we recommend a 4-week POC: week 0 setup, week 1 integration, week 2 validation, week 3 iterate and finalize. That fits your six-week desire if we parallelize setup.
[03:44] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Who will be our primary contacts during the pilot?
[03:49] Jordan Lee: I'll be primary CSM lead. Priya is your SE. For billing/contact it's me and our account team.
[03:58] Priya Nair: For the tech deep dive we'll cover KV cache behavior, batching, and quantization choices that impact latency and cost. Expect some notes on model selection too — small vs medium size models and quantized variants.
[04:15] Carlos Rivera: Can you send recommended model profiles for clinical summarization? We want to balance hallucination risk with latency.
[04:22] Priya Nair: Yes — I'll include our model catalog recommendations and quality profiles. We also have evaluation harnesses and prompt sets you can run against your sample data.
[04:34] Dr. Alan Brooks: Regarding validation, we'll need an eval plan and acceptance criteria — confusion, hallucination thresholds, and recall on key fields.
[04:43] Jordan Lee: We'll include a template for evaluation and suggested metrics.
[04:48] Maya Chen: Payment and contract — will you send a statement of work or trial billing?
[04:53] Jordan Lee: We'll send a pricing summary and SOW options after this call. For pilots we can do a time-limited credit or trial invoice depending on procurement.
[05:05] Carlos Rivera: Any competitor considerations? We've looked at Anthropic and Bedrock; curious about differences in observability and token costs.
[05:14] Priya Nair: Observability is a big differentiator — Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdowns and tracing. Cost profiles and batching options are flexible too.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: Quick recap of next steps: Jordan to send runbook and security pack; Priya to schedule technical deep dive and send network checklist; Carlos to share network details and Maya to finalize pilot scope.
[05:40] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the documentation.
[05:46] Jordan Lee: Thanks all; we'll follow up by email and set the deep dive invite.
[05:51] (end)
